subject: Egress hardening sign-off: ACME private endpoint (next steps)
messages:
From: John Patel <john.patel@acme.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint hardening — allowlist & firewall details needed

Hi Soojin,

We're moving into the audit window for our private deployment with Redwood and need a finalized list of outbound IPs/domains and the minimum firewall policy for our egress gateway. Our auditors ask for:

- Exact CIDR ranges and single-IP endpoints you will use (or the control-plane egress hostnames if IPs cannot be pinned)
- Which ports and protocols are required (e.g., 443, 5223 not expected)
- Whether any callbacks will originate from ephemeral public IPs (and how often they rotate)
- Recommendations for DNS allowlisting vs. IP allowlisting and any proxy requirements

We have a freeze in 8 business days for our prod cutover — can you provide a sign-off or a controlled roll plan (canary + fallback) that auditors can accept?

Thanks,
John Patel
Security Ops Lead
Acme Payments

--
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: John Patel <john.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint hardening — allowlist & firewall details needed

John — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our proposed minimal allowlist and a concise firewall rule set (egress-allowlist-v1.csv, firewall-rule-diff.patch). Summary below.

TL;DR: We can provide a pinned set of five static egress IPs for the control plane + an optional FQDN-based endpoint for model downloads. For connectivity from customer VPC to Redwood Private control plane (control/control-plane), only outbound HTTPS (443) from the private endpoint is required. No persistent inbound openings are needed on your side.

Key deliverables attached:
- Static egress IPs (5 addresses) — suitable for org-wide allowlist
- Recommended firewall policy (stateful, allow outbound to the 5 IPs on 443; block all else)
- Fallback plan: if those IPs are unreachable, traffic will route to our regional failover pool (different CIDR, included in attachment)

Notes and decisions we expect you to make:
1) IP vs DNS: For strict audits, IP allowlisting is preferred. We provide both; if you cannot rely on IPs (cloud provider NAT rotation), we recommend allowlisting the provided FQDNs and deploying short-lived egress proxy certificates.
2) NAT & source IP ownership: If your environment performs SNAT at the NAT gateway, we will accept requests from your NAT IPs; we still recommend a dedicated NAT for Redwood egress to simplify tracing.
3) Monitoring: We'll publish metric hooks for handshake failures and TLS errors to the shared dashboard (link in related_links).

Next step: Aditya, can you validate that the 5 IPs are bound to the regional egress gateway and won't change during the next 6 weeks? Marcus, please confirm the canary window and rollout steps so John can present to his audit team.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: egress-allowlist-v1.csv (5 IPs), firewall-rule-diff.patch (recommended iptables/nft rules)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint hardening — allowlist & firewall details needed

Folks — quick infra notes after reviewing the attachment. Quoted below the parts I changed in the patch.

On Tue, 25 Aug 2026 at 11:03, Soojin Lee wrote:
> TL;DR: We can provide a pinned set of five static egress IPs for the control plane + an optional FQDN-based endpoint for model downloads.

Confirmed: the 5 addresses in egress-allowlist-v1.csv are currently allocated to our us-west region egress gateway and are stable for the next 90 days under our allocation window. We will notify customers 30 days prior to any rotation.

Technical clarifications and suggested changes: 
- Replace the single FQDN for model downloads with an internal proxy hostname (models-redwood-us-west.proxy.redwood-inference.net) and recommend customers allow that hostname only via their outbound proxy. This prevents direct DNS-based allowlisting relying on upstream CDNs.
- For stricter networks: recommend a TLS mutual-auth option for the control-plane handshake. We can issue a client cert to Acme with weekly rotation if they require certificate-based allowlist.
- iptables snippet in firewall-rule-diff.patch: I removed the generic "ALLOW 443 to 0.0.0.0/0" rule and replaced it with explicit ACCEPT to our 5 IPs + two failover CIDRs; also added a LOG+DROP default. Patch lines: +ACCEPT tcp --- anywhere anywhere tcp dpt:443 to {IP1,IP2,IP3,IP4,IP5}

Action items:
- Soojin: please confirm you want to surface the mutual TLS option in the customer-facing guide or keep it as an advanced/ops configuration.
- Marissa: coordinate with Acme on the audit packet (we need their confirmation that IPs will be added to corp firewall by EOD Fri).

-Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Patel <john.patel@acme.com>, Security Team <security@acme.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint hardening — allowlist & firewall details needed

John / Acme Security — thanks for the patience.

We've reviewed infra feedback and ACME's requirements. Redwood Signs-off on the following for your audit packet:

1) Final allowlist: the 5 static egress IPs in egress-allowlist-v1.csv are our recommended production set. The file attached to Soojin's email is the canonical list.
2) Firewall policy: stateful outbound allow to those 5 IPs on TCP/443 only. Block all other outbound flows from the Redwood private endpoint.
3) Fallback & rollout: a canary rollout is scheduled across 6% of your traffic for the first 48 hours; full cutover after 7 days if no TLS/handshake errors exceed 0.1%. We will open a shared incident channel and provide automated alerts to your security pager for the canary window.
4) Optional hardening: mutual TLS and dedicated NAT recommendations are documented in the linked guide (see related_links).

Please consider this message the formal sign-off from Redwood. If your auditors need a formatted PDF statement, reply and I'll generate the audit-ready doc with the exact CIDRs and signatory.

Next steps for Acme:
- Confirm addition of the 5 IPs to corporate firewall by EOD Fri (HubSpot task assigned HS-10234).
- Tell us whether you want mutual TLS issued (yes/no) so Aditya can provision certs.

Thanks — looking forward to the cutover.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Accounts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
